entries.definition: Machine-learning inference performed on ultra-low-power, microcontroller-class hardware, typically under one milliwatt.
synonyms_forbidden: edge ML (used only contrastively, for mobile-scale inference)

entries.definition: A microcontroller-class chip: roughly 10-250 MHz clock, well under 1 GB of memory (about two orders of magnitude below smartphone-class ML hardware), often under 50 mW power draw.
entries.note: first used (I.1, informally) slightly before its full definition (B.1); acceptable because I.1 also gives an informal gloss ('MCU-class hardware') and the formal envelope is not needed until Background -- flagged and accepted, see step-14 audit.

entries.definition: Two submission tracks: the closed division fixes the dataset, model, and quality target (only post-training quantization allowed); the open division allows changing dataset, training, or model, with every deviation documented and no mandatory accuracy bar.
Reducing an already-trained model's numeric precision (e.g. to 8-bit integers) without retraining.
Retraining a model while simulating low-precision numerics, so the model compensates for quantization error.

The complete, open-source package for one benchmark: training scripts, a pretrained model, and C code that runs it on the reference board -- both a baseline result and a starting point submitters may modify.
TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers, the runtime the reference implementations use to execute models on the reference board.
A threshold-free accuracy metric; used for anomaly detection because an anomaly score otherwise needs an arbitrarily chosen decision threshold.
The benchmark's latency metric: how many inferences the device completes per second.
The specific hardware being benchmarked in a given run.

rule_check: defined_at <= first_used_at for every entry except 'MCU-class device' (see its noted, accepted exception); no registered term is later replaced by a synonym in the draft (checked in the step-14 term/load audit).
